12.text: with a knife. The inner membrane is also

13.text: removed. Then the skins are stretched by

15.text: peltries are always taken off whole. They are

26.text: Reindeer-skins are stretched on the ground, and their

27.text: edges are held with stones. Sometimes they are pinned

28.text: to the ground with wooden pegs, which allow more strain

29.text: in stretching, and make the skin larger when dried. Seal

30.text: and walrus skins are stretched with cords on rectangular

31.text: frames quite similar to those used in Alaska.¹ Cords are

32.text: passed through holes cut in the edge of the skin. When

33.text: dry, they are folded in compact elongated packages (Fig.

34.text: 143), for the most part identical with those represented

35.text: by Nelson.² Reindeer-skins are simply folded in two or

36.text: rolled together and tied with a piece of cord.
